example_text: Symplocaceae is placed in the Ericales and is most closely related to the Styracaceae (Stevens, AP website, 22 June 2009).
lamina glabrous beneath or rarely finely appressed hairy when young
base attenuate-cuneate narrowed at a 15--60° angle
joined in a long monadelphous tube in subgen. Cordyloblaste
intercostal veins with reticulum distinct beneath
glabrous or hairy and then mentioned in the description
Twigs pubescent to tomentose or tomentellous at least when young
in many species drying yellowish green
midrib impressed above but in Symplocos theaefolia and S. anomala midrib flat or prominent above
petals connate at the very base
only connate at the very base
often crowned by the persistent calyx lobes rarely the lobes caducous
(stout, dark brown, often marked with raised scars)
entire to glandular denticulate with less than 6 glands per cm
but sometimes thick and then often quite hard
(usually only one fertile, the sterile ones filled with air)
monadelphous or pentadelphous and then the bundles alternipetalous
in subgen. Symplocos corolla glabrous but the lobes sometimes ciliolate
flowers subtended by a bract and 2 bracteoles
especially on midrib and lateral veins
or completely divided and possessing the following characters: tube appressed-long dark brown or rusty hirsute
(the number of locules is often not assessed as the stones mostly are aluminium encrusted, and very hard)
(in cases where the embryo is once or twice curved usually only one cell develops)

example_text: sessile or with axis to 0.5 cm long
(in var. curtisii, var. penangiana and often also in var. ernae)
narrowed into the petiole at a 30°–45° angle
drying yellowish green or green or brownish on both surfaces
usually white or yellowish or greenish
lobes connate only at the base
with c. 5(--10) high ridges or ribs
style often becoming 1--2 mm longer than corolla
